question:
Select the most appropriate idiomatic expression to fill in the blank.

Anita keeps on repeating that she is innocent, but there is ________.

options.text: no pulling up of the socks

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiomatic expression **"no smoke without fire"** means that if there are rumors or signs of something, there is usually some truth to them. (जहां धुआं होता है, वहां आग भी होती है)

 
 
• **Example: **People are saying that the company is in trouble, and you know there's no smoke without fire.
 
 
 
• **"No smoke without fire"** is used to indicate that there is some basis for rumors or suspicions. (जहां धुआं होता है, वहां आग भी होती है)
 
 
• **Example: **Even though Anita keeps on repeating that she is innocent, there is no smoke without fire.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **No pulling up of the socks** (कोई मेहनत नहीं करना): This phrase does not fit the context as it means not making an effort or not improving performance.

 
 
• **Example:** Despite repeated warnings, there was no pulling up of the socks in his work.
 
 
 
• **No rubbing of the shoulders** (कोई नजदीकी संपर्क नहीं): This phrase is not commonly used and does not fit the context.
 
 
• **Example: **In a professional setting, there should be no rubbing of the shoulders with clients.
 
 
 
• **No love lost between** (कोई प्रेम नहीं): This phrase means that two people do not like each other, which does not fit the context.
 
 
• **Example:** There was no love lost between the two rivals in the competition.
